feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. The evidence is iteration 5 (y = 0.02 m, 0.10 m track, 0.8 kg, 0.16 m body, 0.03 m wheels, kp 2.8, kd 0.35), which gave oval steering_oscillation 0.193, line loss 0 on all tracks, oval progress 0.358, and max_error 0.0622 m. Max_error has sat at 0.061 to 0.064 m in every iteration whatever the track, mass, footprint or row height (iterations 0 to 5), so geometry is not the lever for it. The row move to y = 0.02 m reduced oval oscillation and did not raise line loss, so the reaction point is settled. Iteration 4 (0.8 kg, y = 0.03 m) gave oscillation 0.181 and progress 0.34, which shows inertia is the damping lever. This candidate raises wheel radius to 0.035 m, which is a speed change, so I lower kp to 2.4 and raise kd to 0.4 in the controller to hold the steering gain level. Next race: if oval progress rises above 0.38 with oscillation at or below 0.2, keep the wheel radius and move to base_speed. If oscillation rises above 0.2, the yaw gain from the larger wheel is too high, so the next geometry step is a wider track (0.11 m) with the 0.8 kg mass kept. If progress does not move, the speed gain is not reaching the course, so keep the radius and tune base_speed in the controller rather than changing geometry again.
requested_changes: If oval steering_oscillation stays at or below 0.2 and progress rises above 0.38 (iteration 5 was 0.193 and 0.358): keep wheel_radius 0.035 m and mass 0.8 kg, and do not change the sensor row again, since iteration 5 showed y = 0.02 m gave no line loss.

If oval steering_oscillation rises above 0.2 with wheel_radius 0.035 m (iteration 4 at 0.8 kg gave 0.181; iteration 5 gave 0.193): widen wheel_track to 0.11 m, since yaw gain per command has risen with radius and falls as the track widens, and keep 0.8 kg for the damping that iteration 4 showed.

If max_error stays at 0.061 to 0.064 m across this race (every iteration so far, including iteration 5 at 0.0622 m): stop changing geometry for max_error, keep the current sensing and mass, and leave the remaining gap to controller gain.
